name: Hendaye Grande Plage
notes: Long sheltered sandy bay that stays small and gentle; the usual fallback when the rest of the coast is too big.

name: Les Deux Jumeaux
notes: Right over mixed rock and sand facing the twin rocks off Pointe Sainte-Anne.

name: Socoa - La Bougie
notes: Needs a very large swell; breaks off the Socoa side of Saint-Jean-de-Luz bay.

name: Sainte-Barbe
notes: Right-hand point over rock at the north headland of Saint-Jean-de-Luz bay, only on big swells.

name: Erromardie
notes: Reef with a central left and a right; strong local crew.

name: Lafitenia
notes: Long, regular right-hand point break below the cliff; one of the best rights on the Basque coast.

name: Cenitz
notes: Reef cove with an easy left and a playful right bowl, best at high tide.

name: Avalanche
notes: Big-wave left over an outer reef off Guéthary; only works on large swells.

name: Les Alcyons
notes: Technical left over reef bumps next to Guéthary harbour.

name: Parlementia
notes: Long right over a rock reef that holds big swell; sets are heavier than they look from the shore.

name: Côte des Basques
notes: Historic longboard spot below the cliff; easy at low tide, the beach disappears at high tide.

name: Biarritz Grande Plage
notes: Several peaks in front of the casino with a rip channel used to paddle out.

name: Les Cavaliers
notes: Powerful, hollow sandbank peaks next to the jetties; a regular contest venue.

name: La Barre (Anglet)
notes: Jetty-side peaks at the Adour mouth that hold big swell; strong currents and murky water.

name: Tarnos - La Digue
notes: Powerful jetty-side peaks just north of the Adour mouth; handles south wind.

name: La Piste
notes: Hollow shore-pound beach by the Atlantic Wall bunkers.

name: Le Prévent
notes: Fast, hollow peaks close to the Capbreton canyon; strong currents in big swell.

name: Hossegor - La Sud
notes: Sheltered by the Capbreton jetty; the schools' fallback in big swell.

name: La Gravière
notes: Heavy, hollow beach break and WSL venue; thick barrels on solid west swells.

name: La Nord
notes: Outer sandbank north of La Gravière that holds the largest swells in Hossegor.

name: Vieux-Boucau
notes: Shifting sandbanks with strong currents; the south beach is the most powerful.

name: Moliets Plage
notes: Exposed beach break by the golf course and the Huchet mouth; can barrel with offshore wind.

name: Le Truc Vert
notes: Hollow, fast sandbank peaks with unstable banks and strong currents.

name: Lacanau La Nord
notes: Long right off the sandbank in front of the surf club; kiting is only allowed outside lifeguarded hours.

name: Le Gurp
notes: Hollow beach break that locals use when the rest of the Côte d'Argent is maxed out.

name: Soulac-sur-Mer
notes: Smaller, punchy waves near the Gironde mouth with strong tidal currents.

name: Pontaillac
notes: Sheltered Royan cove with mellow waves for learning.

name: La Coubre
notes: Fast shore break with strong longshore currents at the tip of the Côte Sauvage.

name: Bonne Anse
notes: Sheltered lagoon behind the La Coubre sand spit used for kite and windsurf rather than surf.

name: Vert-Bois
notes: Oléron's most consistent beach break.

name: Chassiron
notes: Technical reef at the northern tip of Oléron with strong currents.

name: Les Boulassiers
notes: Left over a rocky reef on the sheltered north-east shore; works on big winter swells.

name: Le Petit Bec
notes: Fast, powerful beach break on Ré's north-west tip that needs a north-west swell.

name: Longeville - Les Conches
notes: Hollow, powerful beach break and contest venue in front of the Bud Bud pines.

name: Tanchet
notes: Sandy bay between two rock platforms; the main surf beach of Les Sables-d'Olonne.

name: Les Sables - Grande Plage
notes: Sheltered town bay that only breaks in bigger swells; a surf channel is set aside in summer.

name: Brétignolles - Les Dunes
notes: Multi-peak beach break that works at most tides depending on the banks.

name: La Sauzaie
notes: Fast, hollow reef break, a rarity on this coast; crowded when it works.

name: Préfailles - Pointe Saint-Gildas
notes: Hollow reef at the point that only works on big swell with offshore wind.

name: La Govelle
notes: Mixed reef and sand on the Côte Sauvage between Batz and Le Pouliguen; sharp mussel-covered rocks.

name: Le Loch
notes: Guidel's main beach break with a right along the north cliff and a long left at the south end.

name: Fort-Bloqué
notes: Long beach sheltered by the fort and reef; the local kite and windsurf hub.

name: Les Kaolins
notes: Heavy, shallow right and hollow left over rock; experts only.

name: Toulhars
notes: Larmor-Plage's winter fallback in storms.

name: Petite Mer de Gâvres
notes: Shallow tidal lagoon, flat water for kite and windsurf.

name: Barre d'Étel
notes: Sandbar waves at the ria mouth with very strong tidal currents and boat traffic.

name: Mané Guen
notes: Backup for the Quiberon Côte Sauvage; smaller in the south under the Portivy reefs.

name: Penthièvre
notes: Beach break by the fort at the isthmus; the fallback when the Côte Sauvage is too big.

name: Port Bara
notes: The most consistent Côte Sauvage cove; strong currents and rocks, not lifeguarded.

name: Belle-Île - Donnant
notes: West-facing island beach that picks up most swells, usually bigger than the mainland.

name: Le Letty
notes: Lagoon behind the dune that floods at high tide; flat water and strong channel current.

name: Pors Carn
notes: Fallback for La Torche when the Baie d'Audierne is too big; reef waves offshore on the left at mid tide.

name: La Torche
notes: Brittany's best-known beach break, north of the point; a rip next to the rocks helps paddle out.

name: Penhors
notes: Peaks along the beach and a reef wave by the small harbour at high tide.

name: Île aux Vaches
notes: Big-wave right over a rock plateau off Audierne.

name: Baie des Trépassés
notes: Sandy bay between Pointe du Raz and Pointe du Van; peaks shift with the banks and it closes out when big.

name: La Palue
notes: Crozon's main beach break, almost always has waves; swimming is banned because of the rips.

name: Le Petit Minou
notes: Small cove at the mouth of the Brest roadstead; east side for experienced surfers, schools on the west.

name: Penfoul
notes: Easy sand peak at high tide with a right-hand reef on the north side.

name: La Mauvaise Grève
notes: Sandbank waves at low tide, then a rock peak from mid tide up in front of Moguériec harbour.

name: Le Dossen
notes: North Finistère's best-known spot; waves up to 4 m on big west to north-west swells.

name: Trestraou
notes: Perros-Guirec's bay; regular small waves suited to learning, more power on autumn and winter swells.

name: Trestel
notes: Sheltered bay with soft, long waves on strong north-west swells.

name: Longchamp
notes: Saint-Lunaire beach break with rock slabs that make it hollower; needs a north swell.

name: Le Sillon
notes: Saint-Malo's long town beach; works on big north swells and the tide changes it completely.

name: Capbreton - Le Miramar
notes: Lifeguarded town beach south of the estacade, the usual learning spot in Capbreton.

name: Les Roches Blanches
notes: Fast, hollow left over rock west of the Tréboul beaches.

name: Morgat
notes: Harbour wall right in big south-west swells; the bay in front is a freeride windsurf spot.

name: La Chapelle
notes: Hollow, powerful reef on the coast road between Argenton and Portsall, favoured by bodyboarders.

name: La Grève d'en Bas
notes: Near Cap Fréhel; needs a strong swell from the Channel and works with south-east wind.
